name: corpus-reader
title: corpus-reader: parse a flawed JSONL corpus into documents plus an exact skipped count
interface:
Module `lib/corpus.mjs`.

```stub
export function readCorpus(file: string): { docs: Array<{ id: string, title: string, body: string }>, skipped: number };
```

Semantics:
- The file is read incrementally (chunked), never assuming it fits comfortably in memory,
  and split on "\n"; a trailing "\r" is stripped so CRLF files parse identically.
- A corpus line is any line that is not empty after trimming. Blank / whitespace-only
  lines are file whitespace, not corpus lines: they are neither documents nor skips.
- A corpus line yields a document iff it parses as JSON AND is a non-array object AND
  has `id`, `title` and `body` all of type string. Every other corpus line increments
  `skipped` and is otherwise ignored — reading never throws on malformed content.
- `docs` preserves file order. Extra JSON fields are ignored, not copied.
- Reading a path that does not exist or cannot be opened throws an Error whose message
  contains the path. That is the only failure mode.
nl_description: Robust JSONL ingestion: turns a corpus file whose lines may be truncated JSON, non-objects, or missing fields into the list of usable documents and the exact number of lines that were thrown away. This is the robustness dimension of the search CLI — indexing must survive garbage and report the skip count precisely, because the judge compares that number. Reusable by anything that needs to read the {id,title,body} JSONL format.
